Documentation.Summary: A Work Order is a contract linked to a contingent worker, defining the start and end dates of their engagement. It can be active (valid) or inactive (expired) and is customizable to suit business needs.
Documentation.LongDescription: A Work Order is a contractual agreement established between the vendor providing the contingent workforce and the company. Creating a Work Order is an integral part of the contingent worker hiring process. When a contingent worker is hired, a corresponding Work Order record is created to define the terms of the engagement. The Work Order record includes start and end dates, which specify the duration of the contract. Once the end date is reached, the contingent worker record is automatically terminated unless the contract is extended. Work Orders can exist in two states: Active, representing contracts that are currently valid, and Inactive, representing contracts that have expired. The Work Order object can be used in its default configuration or customized to meet specific business requirements.

Documentation.Summary: Vendor Info stores key details about external businesses or contractors providing goods or services, including contact, tax, and payment data. It supports compliance, financial oversight, and efficient management of external vendors.
Documentation.LongDescription: Vendor Info represents the details of an external business, organization, or contractor that provides goods or services to your company, particularly in the context of the contingent workforce. Vendor Info creation and maintenance is a key part of managing external service providers. Each Vendor Info record can contain essential details such as the vendor’s name, address, contact information, tax IDs, bank details, and other business or accounting data. This information supports compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, enables accurate financial oversight, and ensures that payment and tax details are properly managed. By centralizing vendor data in the Vendor Info object, businesses can streamline hiring, onboarding, and ongoing management of external vendors, improving both operational efficiency and compliance. Vendor Info entries remain valid until updated or deactivated as part of standard vendor management processes.
